title: Gulf of Maine temperature shock
region: Northeastern United States / Gulf of Maine
observation: In Holyoke’s Salem air-temperature series, daily average and low temperatures in 1816 were more than one standard deviation lower, while daily temperature differential was more than one standard deviation higher, than the other years in the 1814–1818 comparison.
uncertainty: Salem air-temperature observations provide regional context; these are not direct sea-temperature measurements or a Gulf-wide instrumental network.
sourceLocator: Alexander et al., results and temperature-series methods

title: Migratory fish populations respond
observation: Abnormal temperatures affected alewives, shad, herring and mackerel differently according to migration/spawning phenology and temperature tolerance; alewives were particularly affected.
uncertainty: Species responses are inferred from fisheries records, air temperatures and later phenological knowledge; direct fish behavior and mortality were not measured in 1816.

title: Food pressure shifts fishing effort
observation: Crop failure and threat of famine increased pressure on fisheries; insufficient alewife runs contributed to fishers shifting effort toward mackerel, making 1816 remembered as the 'mackerel year'.

title: Temporary shock produces structural fishery change
observation: The shift from riparian toward marine fisheries persisted and expanded after temperatures moderated and alewife populations recovered, indicating a lasting human-system adaptation after the short climate shock.

title: Extremely cold summer in the Czech Lands
observation: Instrumental and documentary evidence records an extremely cold summer in 1816; documentary evidence also records damaging weather and poor grain harvests.

title: Harvest losses become grain-price pressure
observation: Bad grain harvests associated with the 1815–1816 weather were followed by widespread grain-price increases culminating in 1817.

title: Persistent rain in southwestern Bohemia
observation: Václav Jan Mašek of Řenče reports rain beginning 8 June 1816 and continuing for about eight weeks with few rain-free days; wet cereals, poor yields, rising prices and hunger were reported.
uncertainty: Local documentary account; not a measured regional rainfall total.

title: Tambora eruption as an antecedent global shock
observation: The April 1815 eruption of Mount Tambora injected volcanic material into the atmosphere and is identified as a major contributor to the unusually cold 1816 summer in much of Europe and other Northern Hemisphere climate anomalies.

title: Geneva summer afternoons shift 3–4°C colder
observation: Compared with the 1799–1821 reference period, the distribution of afternoon summer temperature anomalies in Geneva shifted by roughly 3–4°C toward colder conditions; increased cloudiness contributed substantially to the pattern.

title: Exceptional Alpine snow storage
observation: Historical reports and hydrological reconstruction indicate substantial snow storage in 1816 and 1817; snowfall events reached unusually low elevations and snow conditions helped set up the hydrological sensitivity of 1817.

title: Lake Constance and Rhine flooding in 1817
place: Rhine at Basel and Lake Constance
observation: On 6–7 July 1817 major flooding affected the Rhine at Basel and Lake Constance; Lake Constance reached the highest documented flood level in the cited reconstruction. Snowmelt combined with intense rainfall was central to the event.

title: Southern China experiences unusual cold, frost and snow
observation: Tree-ring and Chinese documentary proxies show a Tambora-era cold excursion with severe frost damage and snow and ice accumulations unusual for southern China.
sourceLocator: Gao et al., Table 1 and section 3.1
uncertainty: Reported snow and ice include late 1815–January 1816; events are not all confined to calendar 1816.

title: China hydroclimate signal is spatially uneven
observation: Tree-ring drought reconstructions indicate drying tendencies consistent with weakened monsoonal circulation, while documentary drought and flood records show much milder responses outside southern China. The divergence is itself important evidence about proxy sensitivity and regional variation. A multiproxy precipitation reconstruction also lacks a strong response, reinforcing the disagreement across evidence systems.
uncertainty: Drying is not uniformly supported across regions or reconstruction methods.

title: Laennec invents the stethoscope
observation: René-Théophile-Hyacinthe Laennec developed mediate auscultation in 1816 by using a rolled paper tube to transmit chest sounds; he then spent several years refining the instrument and correlating clinical signs with pathology.

title: Frankenstein begins in the cold, stormy summer of 1816
observation: Mary Godwin conceived the story that became Frankenstein during the cold, rainy summer near Geneva; surviving Notebook A contains draft material written from August to early December 1816.

title: United Provinces declare independence
historicalEntity: United Provinces of the Río de la Plata
observation: On 9 July 1816 the Congress of Tucumán declared the formal break of the United Provinces from the Spanish monarchy; the declaration formed part of the wider Spanish American independence process.

title: Treaty of Sugauli ratified
historicalEntity: Kingdom of Nepal / East India Company
observation: The Treaty of Sugauli was exchanged/ratified on 4 March 1816 after the Anglo-Nepalese War. Its articles recognized territorial cessions to the East India Company and provided for accredited ministers between the two states.

title: Anglo-Dutch fleet bombards Algiers
observation: An Anglo-Dutch fleet under Edward Pellew bombarded Algiers on 27 August 1816 after demands for the release of captives were not met. Royal Museums Greenwich records that 1,083 Christian slaves and the British consul were subsequently liberated and restitution and peace terms secured.

title: Shaka assumes AmaZulu chieftaincy and begins expansion
observation: Following the death of Senzangakhona in 1816, Shaka returned and took the AmaZulu chieftaincy. Scholarly chronology describes campaigns and incorporation of nearby chiefdoms during 1816–1817 as part of an expanding political formation.

title: Slachter’s Nek rebels executed
observation: Five men convicted after the 1815 Slachter’s Nek rebellion were publicly hanged on 9 March 1816. The episode later acquired substantial political memory among Afrikaners, though interpretations of its longer-term causal importance differ.

title: The Barber of Seville premieres
observation: Rossini's Il Barbiere di Siviglia premiered at Rome's Teatro Argentina on 20 February 1816. Its opening night was poorly received, but a revised Bologna performance in August was highly successful, preceding rapid wider diffusion.

title: Ashfall devastates Sumbawa croplands
observation: Heavy tephra fall devastated croplands around Tambora; pyroclastic flows reached the sea on the Sanggar Peninsula.
uncertainty: Spatial damage is summarized; no district yield series is available here.

title: Famine and disease follow the local eruption
topic: Famine and disease follow the local eruption
observation: Reports and later scholarship describe starvation and disease after the eruption on Sumbawa and neighboring islands.
uncertainty: Approximate 1815 aftermath; persistence into 1816 is unresolved. No independently measured annual mortality total is supplied.

title: Rice relief and distress livestock sales on Sumbawa
historicalEntity: Sumbawa island polities / British administration in Java
topic: Rice relief and distress livestock sales on Sumbawa
evidenceType: Contemporary documentary report via scholarly review
observation: A report reproduced in scholarship describes people exchanging livestock for small amounts of staples and an official rice gift to the ruler of Sanggar.
uncertainty: Approximate 1815 aftermath; day and month not established here. Colonial report offers a local snapshot; wider relief effectiveness is unresolved.
sourceLocator: Oppenheimer pp. 248–249; Philipps report via Raffles (1817, 1830)

title: Dry conditions reconstructed across monsoon Asia
topic: Dry conditions reconstructed across monsoon Asia
observation: The Monsoon Asia Drought Atlas reconstruction indicates dry conditions in India and Southeast Asia during May–September 1816.
uncertainty: Proxy reconstruction is spatially broad; it does not establish local rainfall totals, harvest losses or famine.
sourceLocator: p. 7, discussion of Monsoon Asia Drought Atlas

title: Macquarie orders punitive expeditions
historicalEntity: Dharawal, Dharug and Gandangara peoples / New South Wales colony
observation: Macquarie issued instructions for military expeditions against Aboriginal people, authorizing violence and hostage-taking.
uncertainty: Colonial records encode the administration’s viewpoint; orders and subsequent conduct must be distinguished. Instructions dated 9 April are distinct from the governor’s 10 April diary entry.

title: Appin massacre
historicalEntity: Dharawal people / New South Wales colony
observation: Wallis’s detachment attacked a sleeping Aboriginal group near the Cataract River, killing men, women and children.
uncertainty: Official death toll of 14 is a minimum in the museum account; the full toll remains uncertain.
sourceLocator: Captain Wallis diary and museum comparison

title: Colonial proclamation restricts Aboriginal movement
historicalEntity: Aboriginal peoples / New South Wales colony
observation: Macquarie issued a proclamation on 4 May restricting Aboriginal movement, gatherings and weapons; principal weapons and gathering controls were to take effect on 4 June.
uncertainty: Policy text establishes imposed rules; enforcement and local responses need separate records. Issuance is distinct from effective dates and actual enforcement.

title: Army of the Andes command and training
historicalEntity: United Provinces of the Río de la Plata
topic: Army of the Andes command and training
observation: San Martín was appointed commander of the Army of the Andes in August; units entered the El Plumerillo training camp in September.
uncertainty: Chronology establishes preparation; supply volumes and labor contributions need additional sources.

title: Army crosses Andean passes
observation: Multiple columns departed Cuyo in January and crossed the Andes; the army assembled west of the mountains in February.
uncertainty: Date range includes several routes and departures rather than one crossing day.

title: Victory at Chacabuco
historicalEntity: Army of the Andes / Spanish royalist forces
observation: San Martín’s army defeated royalist forces commanded by Maroto at Chacabuco.
uncertainty: Victory alone does not establish the later independence outcome or explain all military causes.

title: Amsterdam staple prices surge
observation: Rye prices more than doubled; potato prices rose still more during the crisis.
uncertainty: Commodity-specific city series; no national household average is implied.

title: Delft inventories grain stocks
observation: Delft authorities inventoried merchants’ and bakers’ grain stocks following a provincial request.
uncertainty: An inventory establishes administrative action, not adequate reserves.

title: Dutch public grain purchases face shipping lag
observation: Government-backed grain purchases used commercial networks, but much stock arrived only in late spring or summer 1817.
evidenceType: Government and merchant records analyzed in scholarship
uncertainty: Imports alone do not establish effective price relief.

title: Subsidized rye authorized for Amsterdam
observation: A royal decree reserved 500 lasts of rye for reduced-price sales to poorer Amsterdam residents.
uncertainty: Authorization does not measure delivery or household benefit.

title: Swiss potato losses estimated by crop model
observation: Reconstructed cold and reduced irradiance produce simulated potential potato-yield reductions of 20–50% in 1816.
uncertainty: Model uses current cultivars; this is not a measured historical harvest series.

title: Swiss crop sensitivity differs by species
observation: Winter barley had smaller simulated losses than potatoes. Maize was more sensitive in simulations, but was not yet common locally.
uncertainty: Differences suggest potential buffers; realized crop diversification is not established.

title: Swiss malnutrition gradient exceeds modeled yield pattern
observation: The documented east–west malnutrition gradient was not explained by modeled biophysical yield limits alone; social, economic and political differences mattered.
evidenceType: Historical evidence compared with model simulation
uncertainty: Waterlogging may contribute; the model does not isolate every social factor.

title: European cold anomaly has model-dependent volcanic attribution
observation: Model experiments make the European cold anomaly markedly more likely with volcanic forcing; the increase varies by model and forcing estimate.
uncertainty: The headline increase of up to about 100 times is a model result, not a uniform regional probability.

title: European wetness can emerge from circulation variability
observation: Circulation analogues reproduce much anomalous wetness without volcanic forcing; simulations nevertheless increase wet-summer likelihood by roughly 1.5–3 times with forcing.
uncertainty: Temperature and rainfall have different attribution strengths; precipitation must not be assigned to Tambora alone.

title: Jefferson records a cold Virginia spring
observation: Jefferson reports morning temperatures averaging 53°F so far in May, against 63°F in other years, and one morning at 43°F.
evidenceType: Contemporary instrumental observations reported in correspondence
uncertainty: Partial month and unspecified reference years; not a daily all-hours or regional mean.
unit: degrees Fahrenheit, reported partial-month morning mean

title: Frost damages early fruits in Virginia
observation: Jefferson reports repeated frosts killing early fruits and expects poor tobacco and wheat crops.
uncertainty: Fruit damage is reported; the wheat/tobacco statement is a forecast, not a final yield count.

title: Monticello rainfall report shows severe seasonal dryness
observation: Jefferson reports one-third inch of June rain against a 3¾-inch average, and 0.8 inch in August against a 9⅙-inch average.
evidenceType: Contemporary instrumental observations reported in correspondence
uncertainty: Reported amounts and historical baselines retain the letter’s wording; not a standardized modern climatology or regional mean.
baseline: Jefferson’s stated June/August averages, drawn from Notes on the State of Virginia

title: Jefferson forecasts an Atlantic-state maize shortfall
place: Atlantic states, as described from Virginia
observation: Jefferson reports August frost damage to corn beyond the mountains and forecasts an Atlantic-state corn crop below one-third of an ordinary crop.
uncertainty: Contemporary estimate, not an independently compiled realized harvest statistic.

title: Good Korean rice harvest despite wider climate disruption
observation: 1816 barley suffered no significant loss; rice harvests were good. Only 17 of 336 prefectures reported poor yields; tax-exempt paddies were 11.2% of assessed area.
evidenceType: Administrative crop/tax records analyzed in scholarship
sourceLocator: Section 3, paragraphs 2–5; Figure 2; Annual Crop Reports in Sŭngjŏngwŏn ilgi
uncertainty: Administrative categories and taxation proxies are not crop tonnage; good aggregate conditions do not rule out local hardship. Paddy-tax figures cover six assessed provinces; harvest reporting spans eight.
peerReview: Targeted independent cross-check of Asia/health and Americas/Oceania research; original records accessed as described by sources.

title: Seoul rainfall reconstruction shows a wet 1816
observation: Seoul rain-gauge reconstruction gives 1,880 mm in 1816, 48.3% above the cited 1910–1945 average. July–August contributed 1,322 mm.
uncertainty: Seoul station cannot stand for the whole peninsula; reference-period comparison does not isolate volcanic forcing.
peerReview: Targeted independent cross-check of Asia/health and Americas/Oceania research; original records accessed as described by sources.

title: Korean rice harvest classified normal in 1817
observation: 1817 rice harvest was classified normal overall; 66 prefectures reported crop failures, and tax exemptions covered 18.8% of assessed paddy area.
evidenceType: Administrative crop/tax records analyzed in scholarship
uncertainty: A normal national classification does not mean every region or crop was unaffected; this is 1817 aftermath context. Paddy-tax denominator concerns six assessed provinces.
peerReview: Targeted independent cross-check of Asia/health and Americas/Oceania research; original records accessed as described by sources.

title: Korean famine and price crisis precede Tambora
observation: The 1814–1815 famine followed drought and uneven rainfall in 1814. Local rice prices in summer 1815 were reported about 808–866% above usual levels.
sourceLocator: Section 4; Figure 5; diary-based local market prices
uncertainty: The 1814 crop crisis predates Tambora; no Tambora causal edge is justified. Local prices are not a national price index.
peerReview: Targeted independent cross-check of Asia/health and Americas/Oceania research; original records accessed as described by sources.

title: Kumaun winter–spring drought reconstructed from cedar rings
observation: Himalayan cedar reconstruction ranks 1816 as the driest SPI7-May year of 1720–2012, with SPI −1.92; the calibration explains 60% of observed index variance.
sourceLocator: Sections 2.5 and 3.1, printed p.118; Table 5 p.120
uncertainty: Seven-month November–May index is not summer-monsoon rainfall. No direct 1816 harvest/price measurement is supplied; Tambora attribution remains an interpretation.
peerReview: Targeted independent cross-check of Asia/health and Americas/Oceania research; original records accessed as described by sources.

title: Jessore cholera reported in August 1817
observation: Assistant surgeon R. Tytler reported Jessore's cholera outbreak to magistrate Charles Chapman on 23 August 1817.
evidenceType: Colonial medical/judicial records analyzed in scholarship
sourceLocator: Footnote 104: Tytler to Chapman, 23 August 1817, British Library APAC F/4/678
uncertainty: A report date does not establish the first infection or a new pathogen origin; Tambora is not demonstrated as a cause.
dateBasis: Report/letter date, not necessarily event onset.

title: Fear of cholera prompts flight from Jessore
observation: By late August 1817 Chapman described widespread flight from Jessore in fear of cholera; reports principally represented European and official experience.
evidenceType: Colonial medical/judicial records analyzed in scholarship
sourceLocator: Retelling around footnotes 38–39; paragraph beginning 'The exact toll of human life...'
uncertainty: Colonial observers do not enumerate all residents. Fear-driven movement is supported; its transmission effect is not measured here.

title: Calcutta magistrate describes uneven cholera exposure
observation: Magistrate John Eliot reported cholera concentrated in low-lying districts and suburbs, describing crowding by migrants from the countryside.
evidenceType: Colonial medical/judicial records analyzed in scholarship
sourceLocator: Paragraph around footnote 107; Eliot to Bayley, 15 September 1817, BL APAC F/4/678
uncertainty: Observation of locality is not proof that elevation, crowding or weather caused disease. Modern waterborne mechanisms need separate evidence.
dateBasis: Report/letter date, not necessarily event onset.

title: Retrospective account links Irish scarcity and fever
observation: An 1846 parliamentary account recalled deficient 1816 grain and potato crops, scarce turf and bedding straw, and fever becoming prevalent in summer 1817.
sourceLocator: 17 February 1846 debate; paragraph beginning 'He now came to 1817'; lines 170–172 on official page
uncertainty: The food–fever interpretation is the speaker's. Do not equate all historical fever with confirmed epidemic typhus or assign a precise Tambora mortality toll.
peerReview: Targeted independent cross-check of Asia/health and Americas/Oceania research; original records accessed as described by sources.

title: Dublin fever hospital reports insufficient capacity
observation: Cork Street physicians asked for more hospital capacity in 1818, reporting delays of days for admission and deaths among patients waiting.
sourceLocator: 1818 government correspondence; Barker and Cheyne 1821, pp.247–250, as transcribed by institutional history
uncertainty: Aftermath observation; no count of waiting-list deaths is verified. Does not quantify national mortality or isolate nutrition from transmission.

evidenceType: Colonial documentary accounts via scholarly synthesis
sourceLocator: Printed p.49, paragraph citing Bataviasche Courant 26 October 1816
uncertainty: Report date does not identify disease or count mortality; Boers accessed colonial records. Direct-ash and subsequent food/epidemic effects are distinct.

evidenceType: Colonial documentary accounts via scholarly synthesis
sourceLocator: Printed p.49, notes 76–77: Van den Broek 1835 pp.165,183; Olivier 1827 p.451

evidenceType: Colonial documentary accounts via scholarly synthesis
sourceLocator: Printed p.49, note 78, citing Vickers 1989 p.67 and Linda Connor communication

title: French artists arrive in Rio de Janeiro
historicalEntity: United Kingdom of Portugal, Brazil and the Algarves
observation: French artists arrived at Rio aboard the Calphe from Le Havre on 26 March; the Gazeta reported their arrival on 6 April.
sourceLocator: Opening paragraph under A missão artística francesa; cites Gazeta do Rio de Janeiro, 6 April 1816
uncertainty: The later label 'mission' does not establish that all artists arrived under a single formal state invitation.

title: Dutch mission reaches the Asante court
observation: Sheales places Willem Huydecoper’s arrival in Kumase on 22 May 1816, after Daendels dispatched him to negotiate for the Dutch trading interests.
sourceLocator: Printed p43; Daendels1815–1817 [1964], p111 and p242
uncertainty: European company correspondence frames the mission; Asante intentions require separate evidence. Dispatch dates differ between narrative and diary bibliographies; retain arrival date only.

title: Asante ruler questions interruption of imported silverware
observation: Huydecoper’s 24 May diary records the Asantehene asking why fine silverware no longer arrived; the envoy attributed the interruption to recent warfare and said reopened sea routes would restore supply.
uncertainty: The supply explanation is the envoy’s contemporary explanation, not independently measured shipping volume. No Tambora connection.

title: Daendels sends imported silver as a diplomatic gift
observation: Sheales reports that Daendels sent the Asantehene a silver cup received from Holland in December 1816.
uncertainty: December dates receipt of the cup; exact dispatch date is unspecified. Diplomatic rivalry is scholarly interpretation. Stored year refers to the receipt/dispatch episode; no exact dispatch month is asserted.

title: Dispatch reports Radama’s relatives in Mauritius
observation: Farquhar’s12September 1816 dispatch reports the arrival in Mauritius of two young relatives whom he describes as Radama’s brothers, and plans closer relations with Madagascar.
sourceLocator: Chapter4, reproduced letter beginning In a letter from the Mauritius dated September12th1816
uncertainty: The date is the dispatch date, not necessarily arrival. Other historical accounts describe nephews: retain the source’s designation as attributed language until identities are resolved. Colonial language about civilization is authorial rhetoric.
dateBasis: Dispatch date; arrival occurred by this date.

title: Lesage mission connects Mauritius and Imerina
observation: Valette identifies Captain Lesage’s mission to Radama as spanning November 1816–April 1817.
sourceLocator: Printed p572, footnote1, reference to Valette’s1969 study La mission du capitaine Lesage auprès de Radama Ier
uncertainty: Month-range mission chronology; no agricultural or climate effects established.

title: Preliminary Radama–Lesage agreement
observation: Valette examines the peace agreement reported as concluded between Radama and Lesage on4February 1817, with subsequent approval by the governor of Mauritius envisaged.
sourceLocator: Printed p572, opening paragraph and Ellis quote; Ellis1838 History of Madagascar II p158
uncertainty: Do not conflate this preliminary agreement with23October 1817 anti-slave-export treaty. First page reports earlier authors; remaining article should be checked before asserting exact legal scope.

title: Radama prohibits slave export through a treaty proclamation
observation: Rossi identifies Radama’s23October 1817 proclamation as an anti-slave-trade treaty signed at Tamatave by his commissioners and approved by Farquhar.
sourceLocator: Section The Problem of Apparent Homogeneity, Madagascar discussion; footnotes56–59
uncertainty: Legal prohibition does not demonstrate effective enforcement or abolition of domestic slavery. Promised agricultural benefits in the text are political claims, not proof of famine or successful cultivation.

title: Atlantic–Indian shipping routes show modest 1816 cooling
region: Atlantic and Indian Ocean East India Company shipping corridors
place: Atlantic and Indian Ocean East India Company shipping corridors
observation: East India Company ship thermometer records place 1816 as the coldest annual value in the1794–1833 regional series, about0.6°C below that period’s average.
evidenceType: Marine air-temperature instrumental records analyzed in scholarship
sourceLocator: Raible2016 Climate response in observations, marine paragraphs citing Brohan2012 ref52; Brohan2012 abstract describes900 logbooks and273000 weather records
uncertainty: Shipboard air temperature, not sea-surface temperature; coverage follows trade routes, not a complete basin average. Instrument practices and sampling matter.

title: Indian Ocean coral reconstructions include a cold 1807–1816 interval
observation: Tierney’s Indian Ocean reconstruction ensemble shows 1807–1816 about0.8°C below1961–1990, with cooling present in multiple coral series.
sourceLocator: Section3.1 Indian Ocean, printed p233; target definition p231
uncertainty: All early nineteenth-century coral records useδ18O, also sensitive to seawater isotopes/salinity. CE validation is below zero before 1840. This is a decade average, not an 1816 measurement or proof of Tambora-only causation.
extendedContextReason: Multi-year proxy baseline overlaps 1816; retained to avoid inventing an annual value.
unit: degrees Celsius, approximate decadal SST reconstruction anomaly

title: Greenland Sea 1816–1817 contrasts with distant cooling
observation: Scoresby’s voyage observations show summers 1816 and 1817 warmer and less ice-covered than the preceding years in the Greenland Sea.
evidenceType: Contemporary ship logs analyzed in scholarship
sourceLocator: Abstract p315; section2 p316; Figure2 p317
uncertainty: Relative to preceding voyages, not proof the basin was warmer than a modern baseline. Routes followed the ice edge; measurement exposure is imperfectly documented. Do not infer Tambora caused local warming.

title: Modelled upper-ocean cooling persists into 1816–1817
observation: CESM Last Millennium Ensemble simulations peak in upper100m cold anomalies in early 1816 and full-depth ocean heat loss near7×10²²J in 1817.
sourceLocator: Results Figures5–6; Methods Model runs describes18 volcanically forced members
uncertainty: Simulation output, not direct historical ocean measurement. Regional response, aerosol forcing, model physics and earlier 1809 forcing remain uncertain. Supports an ocean-memory mechanism, not quantified historical maritime economic harm.

title: Méduse expedition and delayed Saint-Louis restoration
historicalEntity: Saint-Louis / French and British colonial administrations
observation: UNESCO’s nomination chronology records the 1816 Méduse expedition to recover Saint-Louis and return occurring only in 1817. BCEAO dates France’s renewed presence to25June 1817.
sourceLocator: UNESCO AnnexI Aperçu historique,1816 entry; BCEAO VolumeI p129 SectionI
